items.title: The hardest model test: pushback that's based on something
items.summary: ◆ The Take: For a long time, models weren't much better than writing on paper because every idea was the best idea ever. PHP's Volker Dusch called it the most severe security issue the language has faced in over a decade, comparing it to 2014's Heartbleed.

items.title: Walmart opens the doors to third-party shopping agents
items.summary: Business: While Amazon, JPMorgan, and Bank of America say no, Walmart will let customers link personal agents with configurable spending limits starting next month — surprising given its proprietary Sparky agent already drives order values 40% higher than non-agentic shoppers. items.title: Bubble calls have been wrong every year — carry salt anyway
items.summary: ◆ The Take: The bubble-burst narrative recurs around this time every year: 2024's scaling-wall panic preceded the first reasoning models, and last year's 'enterprises won't keep paying' fears — embodied in the MIT 95%-of-pilots-fail report — preceded enterprise spend booming at around 50% a quarter. Previous calls being wrong doesn't make future ones wrong too; it just means every bombastic headline deserves a bag of salt while we wait for the Anthropic IPO to deliver a more definitive answer.
